summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish a new refundable tax credit of up to $5,000 for qualified child care startup expenses incurred by licensed family child care providers operating primarily out of their homes.

scores.thoughts: This bill establishes a new refundable tax credit, which effectively acts as a government expenditure by reducing tax revenue and potentially leading to direct payments from the government to taxpayers. This increases government spending.

The bill creates a new refundable tax credit for qualified child care startup expenses, which reduces the tax liability for eligible taxpayers. This constitutes a reduction in taxes for those who qualify.

By introducing a new refundable tax credit, the bill is likely to decrease government revenue or increase outlays, which would contribute to the national debt if not offset by other measures. The bill does not include any provisions for offsetting these costs.

The bill creates a new refundable tax credit (up to $5,000 per qualified taxpayer) for child-care startup expenses with no offsetting revenue measures or spending cuts. This directly increases federal outlays, pushing the bill toward accepting larger deficits to fund child-care priorities.
